model.title: Strategic Grazing to Reduce Risk of Wildfire Act
model.meta: Energy and Natural Resources Committee · Sen. Catherine Cortez Masto (D-NV)

summary.text: The bill would require the Secretary of Agriculture and the Secretary of the Interior to develop, within 18 months of enactment, a strategy for using livestock grazing to reduce wildfire risk on federal lands they manage. The strategy would consider grazing on vacant allotments during droughts, wildfires, or other disasters, targeted grazing to reduce dry vegetation and invasive grasses such as cheatgrass, and grazing in post-fire recovery. It would also consider using advanced tools such as virtual fencing, avoiding conflicts with other land uses, and cooperative agreements with states, tribes, and local firefighting agencies. The Secretaries would coordinate with states, wildlife agencies, local governments, tribes, utilities, and firefighters, and post the strategy publicly. Existing grazing programs and the Taylor Grazing Act permit requirements would not be affected.
